name: Lou Arnett
life: “I learned transport planning on the bus I took to two part-time jobs.” Saturday often includes a stop at the entrance to the Wash House, where Lou stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I set the distance in a planning office. My father made me walk it with his groceries.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an unlined tan jacket and a little coil of soft measuring tape. Lou has two dimples that appear only with a full smile, with a long plait tucked inside the collar. Lou looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry during a conversation.
personality: Lou has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To walk the twenty paces with groceries before signing off.
family: Franklin Brandt is Lou’s stepsibling. Lou brings a spare shopping bag. Franklin chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *Spin cycle choir*, Franklin says, “I wanted the noisy bearing replaced. Hearing the song hasn't changed my mind about my night shift.”
connections: Agnes Kahn. The planner learns why the new morning light matters to a lip reader. Also in the story is Stella Hull (access reviewer).

reactions.situation: A driver goes past the old stop in the rain
reactions.response: Lou stays with the stranded rider and helps check the next usable stop.

reactions.situation: An unfamiliar person asks for directions but cannot read the street signs
reactions.response: Lou walks with them as far as the first landmark and points to the next one from there.

reactions.situation: When a private quarrel becomes a public joke
reactions.response: Lou says the plainest truthful thing possible and changes the subject.
